title: Auto Parts Vendor Compliance Deductions at Industrial and Automotive Buyers

# Auto Parts Vendor Compliance Deductions at Industrial and Automotive Buyers


By[Victoria London](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/profile/victoria-london) , *Content Writer*


Last Updated October 15, 2026


7 min read


In this article, learn about:


-


- How commercial and quality compliance differ


The fees and thresholds four buyers publish


How distributors and auto parts retailers enforce rules differently


The dispute windows and evidence each buyer requires


Auto parts vendor compliance means two different things, and most suppliers staff only one. Quality and regulatory compliance covers standards such as[IATF 16949](https://vda-qmc.de/en/iatf/) (the automotive quality standard), production part approval process ([PPAP](https://webstore.ansi.org/standards/aiag/aiagppap2006) ) requirements, and the European[REACH](https://www.baua.de/EN/Topics/Chemicals-biological-agents/Chemicals-law/REACH) chemicals rule.


Commercial compliance covers the rules each buyer sets:


the routing guide, the advance ship notice (ASN) deadline, the fill rate threshold, the pallet specification, and the invoice match. It often falls between departments, and it takes money off a remittance.


## Why Do Quality Standards Not Explain Your Remittance?


Quality standards govern how a part is designed, made, and approved. They do not explain a deduction on a payment. Deductions come from commercial rules: a missing[advanced shipping notice](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/edi-856-ship-notice-manifest) (ASN), a shipment below a fill rate threshold, an invoice that disagrees with the[purchase order](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/what-is-a-purchase-order) (PO), or an item record with the wrong shipping dimensions.


Each buyer sets its own thresholds, codes, and dispute windows. A supplier that can read all three can dispute a deduction with the right evidence.


## What Does Retail Compliance Cost Auto Parts Suppliers?


Retail vendor compliance shows up as fees on the remittance, and each buyer calculates them differently.


### AutoZone Billback Codes and Adjustment Memos


[AutoZone requires invoices through electronic data interchange (EDI)](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/autozone-accounts-payable-adjustment-memos-commercial-accounts-and-vendor-portal-access) and matches each one against its PO automatically. An invoice matches only when item numbers, cost, and quantity agree with the PO. A mismatch produces an adjustment memo with a $25 penalty, filed under cost, quantity, allowances, or Vendor Direct Purchase (VDP) non-match.


Billbacks, the deductions tied to supplier agreements, carry a 10-character number. The first two characters identify the type, and the last eight are assigned in sequence. Four of AutoZone’s published codes are:


Code


What It Charges


FR


Fill rate fees for incomplete shipments


LP


Late POs


VN


Vendor portal access fee


AU


Freight on returned merchandise


AutoZone also starts a return with a chargeback equal to the current cost of the returned items.


### O’Reilly On-Time, In-Full Fines


[O’Reilly expects a 93% on-time, in-full score](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/oreilly-vendor-guide-requirements) . Its published fine structure works like this:


1.


Below 93%, the fine is typically 15% of expected expenses.


2.


Above 93% with late POs, the fine is $100 per late PO.


3.


O’Reilly assesses no fine until the fifth day after the lead time ends (typically 14 calendar days), which leaves four extra days for holidays and delays.


### Home Depot Offsets


[Home Depot’s fines are often called offsets](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/compliance-at-home-depot) , and its published amounts include:


1.


$250 per routing guide violation


2.


$1,000 for a missing ASN and $250 for a late one


3.


$100 per ASN for a wrong or missing transportation management system (TMS) ship ID


4.


A 10% offset on items not received when fill rate falls below 98%


5.


$1,000 per item for out-of-date or inaccurate shipping dimensions in its item data portal


## How Do Distributors Like Grainger Differ?


[Grainger’s published rules](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/graingerfulfillmentguide) put enforcement at the start of the order. A PO must be acknowledged within one business day of creation, and a late acknowledgment can create on-time, in-full problems. A shipment that arrives without an ASN, or with an incomplete one, can be refused.


An item that can’t ship has to come off the ASN entirely, because a zero-quantity line counts as noncompliant. A shipment with more than one trailer needs one ASN per trailer. Grainger says violations can lead to chargebacks or fees, but its guide lists no amounts.


The retail buyers above mostly enforce through fines and offsets on the remittance. Grainger adds a checkpoint at receiving, where a refused shipment can cost a supplier before any deduction is calculated.


## What Else Triggers Deductions in This Category?


Four causes sit outside the fee lists above.


1.


The[current version of the Aftermarket Catalog Exchange Standard (ACES) is 5.0](https://www.autocare.org/aces/) , and the standard communicates product fitment data. The Auto Care Association supports only version 5.0 and version 4.2. Outdated fitment data can send a part to the wrong vehicle and bring it back as a return.


2.


Core returns and warranty credits are covered in a separate[core return program guide](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/core-return-program-for-auto-parts-suppliers-who-want-their-deposits-back) .


3.


[O’Reilly specifies](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/oreilly-vendor-guide-requirements) 48-by-40-inch pallets and a 72-inch maximum load height, including the pallet.


4.


O’Reilly requires hazardous materials to be noted on the bill of lading (BOL). Home Depot applies a $1,000 per item offset for hazmat noncompliance in its item data.


Many deductions start with a document that does not match a buyer’s rules.[Double-checking the PO (EDI 850), ASN (EDI 856), and invoice (EDI 810) before they send](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/edi-chargebacks-explained) catches mismatches upstream.


## How Do You Dispute Each Buyer’s Deductions?


Windows, forms, and evidence differ by buyer.


### Disputing at AutoZone


1. Invoice disputes are due within 18 months of the invoice date, and return disputes within 9 months of the deduction date.


2. Disputes go on AutoZone’s Excel template and are sent tomerch.payable@autozone.com .


3. Cost disputes need category manager approval. Quantity disputes need a distribution center (DC) inventory adjustment report with a 120-day lookback. Allowance disputes need the vendor agreement, and cancelled PO disputes need proof of delivery.


4. AutoZone Accounts Payable researches the claim and may repay in full, repay in part, or deny it. Management approves all settlements.


### Disputing at O’Reilly


O’Reilly takes disputes by email to its vendor compliance mailbox or through supplyLINE, its vendor portal. In supplyLINE:


1. Log in and open Reports.


2. Select Accounts Payable, then Shipping Compliance.


3. Complete the form, which sends the dispute to the mailbox automatically.


A late-shipment dispute needs proof of delivery, the carrier’s name, and an explanation for the delay. A fill rate dispute starts with an exported fill rate report, with two added columns (Supplier Units Shipped and Supplier Dollars Shipped) so the fine can be recalculated. A reversed deduction is repaid with the next payment. O’Reilly’s guide states no dispute deadline.


### Disputing at Home Depot


1.


Transportation offsets are issued in the first week of the month for the previous month, and suppliers have one month to dispute them.


1.


Disputes go through the Supplier Performance Management app in Supplier Hub. Offsets from its rapid distribution centers and direct fulfillment centers must be disputed there, or they are denied automatically.


1.


Evidence can include documentation from a Home Depot employee, a copy of the BOL, a TMS screenshot, a copy of the ASN, and a copy of the label and UPS manifest.


## How Should You Track Retail Vendor Compliance Fees?


A log that records the buyer, the code, the amount, and the PO, ASN, or invoice behind each deduction shows which document keeps triggering the same charge. A code that repeats on the same document type points to a process fix, and a one-time code points to a dispute.


## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is a vendor compliance manual?


A[vendor compliance manual](https://www.spscommerce.com/community/articles/how-to-build-a-vendor-guide-in-2026) is the document a buyer publishes with its operating rules for suppliers, such as packaging, labeling, and EDI requirements. The fees and thresholds in this article come from those published requirements.


### Which ACES version is current?


ACES 5.0 is current,[announced by the Auto Care Association on April 2, 2026](https://www.autocare.org/news/latest-news/details/2026/04/02/auto-care-association-releases-aces--5.0-and-pies--8.0) . ACES 4.2 is the previous version, and the association supports only those two.


### Does retail compliance software help with these deductions?


Retail compliance software can double-check documents against each buyer’s requirements before they send, which catches many of the mismatches behind deductions. The deductions that still arrive need the dispute evidence described above.
